findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a proving step for AC7/AC8: dispatch (or a forced-failure fixture) that asserts the run summary contains a well-anchored `git bisect start <bad> <last-green>` line and a resolved last-green SHA (and that the graceful-degradation branch is taken when history is empty).
evidence: Verification: 'The new policy test under tests/ covering AC 1, 2, 6, 9, 10.' — AC7 and AC8 are absent from the list

AC7/AC8 describe run-summary output that only manifests on a scheduled/dispatched run (and, for the recipe, a FAILING run) — no fixture, forced-failure dispatch, or assertion is described to exercise it
AC11 scopes its assertions to 'the trigger policy' (push-no-match, dispatch, cadences, forbidden set), not summary content
findings.finding: AC7 (failing run emits copy-pasteable bisect recipe) and AC8 (last-known-green SHA published to summary) have no described proving step — the Verification section's policy test explicitly covers only AC 1,2,6,9,10, and AC11's regression coverage is scoped to trigger policy, not summary-output emission.
scenarios: The bisect recipe ships with a shell-expansion bug or wrong SHA range and nobody notices until a real 2am incident
last-green resolution silently returns empty and the 'graceful degradation' path is never actually verified
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AC11/Verification to assert on the emitted summary artifact — e.g. run the summary-generation step against a stub Actions-API response and `grep -E 'git bisect run'` plus a SHA-shaped match, and a second case with empty run history asserting the degraded message rather than a failure.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a concrete cron minute (default) for the 6-hourly schedule, e.g. `17 */6 * * *`, so all three main-health workflows share one deliberate off-the-hour value.
evidence: AC3: 'gain a 6-hourly schedule at a non-zero minute'
findings.finding: The plan does not specify a concrete off-the-hour minute for the 6-hourly schedule; AC3 only requires 'a non-zero minute', deferring the exact value to the executor.
scenarios: Three workflows each pick a different arbitrary minute, or all pick the same minute and pile onto each other
findings.suggested_fix: Pin a specific value in the plan (e.g. minute 17) and note whether the three workflows share it or stagger deliberately.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add test coverage for the AC7/AC8 report logic: assert the bisect recipe is emitted on failure and that last-known-green SHA resolution degrades gracefully (not fail-the-run) when the Actions API returns no prior green run.
evidence: AC8: 'resolved from the workflow's own successful run history via the Actions API ... if it cannot be resolved the report degrades gracefully rather than failing the run'

AC11: 'a test asserts, per workflow, that a push to refs/heads/main does not match, that dispatch remains, that the cadences are as specified, and that the forbidden set is unmodified' — scoped to trigger policy only, not to the report-generation/SHA-resolution logic
Verification section names the policy test covering 'AC 1, 2, 6, 9, 10' — AC7/AC8 report logic is absent from the named test coverage
findings.finding: The plan specifies new runtime report-generation logic (AC7 bisect-recipe emission, AC8 last-known-green SHA resolution from the Actions API with a graceful-degradation branch when resolution fails), but the test plan (AC11) covers only trigger-policy structure — push-to-main matching, dispatch presence, cadences, forbidden-set immutability. The AC8 degradation path ('if it cannot be resolved the report degrades gracefully rather than failing the run') is new conditional logic with a failure branch and no named test coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the tests/ policy suite (or add a focused unit test for the report-summary script) to exercise: (a) the failure path emits a copy-pasteable `git bisect` recipe, and (b) the SHA resolver returns a graceful fallback when no successful prior run exists — using a stubbed/recorded Actions API response so the degradation branch is executed.

findings.checklist_item: Specify that the AC7/AC8 failure-summary + last-green-SHA step is emitted from a NEW caller-level job/step (e.g. a dedicated `main-health-report` job with `if: failure()`/`if: always()` that depends on `build-and-test`), NOT by editing the forbidden reusable, and state which of the scheduled workflows (test/optionality/verify-identity) carry it.
evidence: test.yml: `build-and-test:\n    uses: ./.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` — the gate runs inside the reusable
AC7: 'publishes a copy-pasteable remediation recipe to the run summary'; AC8: 'published in that same summary'
The reusable takes no inputs from the caller (test.yml comment: 'the reusable takes no secrets'), so a caller-defined summary step must live in a separate caller-level job
findings.finding: AC7/AC8 require a failing scheduled run to emit a bisect recipe + last-green SHA to the run summary, but the plan does not say WHERE that step lives; test.yml's actual work is delegated to the reusable _build-and-test.yml (uses: ./.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml), which is in the forbidden byte-identical set (AC10) and accepts no caller steps. A reusable-called job cannot host a summary step defined by the caller, so the recipe must be emitted from a NEW caller-level job/step — the plan should state this to avoid an AC7/AC8-vs-AC10 collision.
findings.location: AC7, AC8, AC10; 'Files this touches'; test.yml job `build-and-test`
scenarios: Implementer tries to add the bisect/last-green summary inside the shared reusable to reach the test output, violating AC10
Implementer adds it only to test.yml's caller but forgets optionality/verify-identity, so their scheduled failures have no recipe
findings.suggested_fix: Add a caller-level job in each scheduled main-health workflow (needs: [build-and-test], if: always()) that writes the bisect recipe (on failure) and last-known-green SHA (always) to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, leaving the reusable _*.yml files untouched.
